correctness.rationale: For every integer r>=2, the frozen RESULT.md constructs B_1=(1+z)^-1, B_r=(1+z/r)^-r, and R_r=(r B_r-B_1)/(r-1). Expansion gives order two; F_r=(1+z/r)^r/(1+z) has (log F_r)'=((r-1)z)/((r+z)(1+z))>0 on z>0, F_r(0)=1<r and F_r→infinity, so precisely one sign transition. Direct rational R_2 simplification gives z_2=2+2sqrt2. Root bound log r<z_r<2 log r (large r) yields z_r=log r+log log r+o(1). Independent exact Fraction computations confirmed the R_2 algebra at 12 sample integers and bisection roots for r=2,3,4,5,8,16,32,64; finite checks are not the universal proof.
